query: For high-entropy alloys intended for extreme environments, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties? State the intervention without limiting its class, the proposed mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the temperature and application boundaries under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment whose outcome would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Thermomechanical processing with optimized parameters can improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of Al0.1CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy by refining the grain structure and introducing nanoscale twins.
generation.intervention: Thermomechanical processing with a true strain of 0.5 at 600°C and optimized parameters
generation.structural_mediator: Grain refinement and formation of nanoscale twins
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and twin boundary hardening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and ductility by 15% compared to the baseline Al0.1CoCrFeNi alloy
generation.baseline: Baseline Al0.1CoCrFeNi alloy without thermomechanical processing
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in mechanical properties may vary depending on the optimized thermomechanical processing parameters and the resulting microstructure.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of Al0.1CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with and without thermomechanical processing at elevated temperatures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermomechanically processed alloy does not show a significant improvement in yield strength and ductility compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

proposals.intervention: Addition of 1 at.% Ti and 1 at.% Mo
proposals.mechanism: Precipitation hardening and solid solution strengthening
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and creep resistance by 20% compared to the baseline Al0.1CoCrFeNi alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The addition of Ti and Mo can enhance the high-temperature mechanical properties of the alloy by forming L12-structured precipitates, which can act as obstacles to dislocation movement, thereby improving the yield strength and creep resistance of the alloy.

proposals.intervention: Surface coating with a 10 μm thick layer of Al2O3

proposals.mechanism: Oxidation resistance and reduction of surface degradation
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxidation resistance and reduction of surface degradation by 30% compared to the uncoated Al0.1CoCrFeNi alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The surface coating can provide a protective barrier against oxidation and surface degradation, thereby improving the high-temperature mechanical properties of the alloy in extreme environments.

proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The addition of B and C can enhance the high-temperature mechanical properties of the alloy by segregating at grain boundaries and reducing grain boundary sliding, thereby improving the creep resistance and yield strength of the alloy.
